entities.summary:
Titus Flavius Vespasianus, Roman emperor from 79 to 81 AD, was a member of the Flavian dynasty. He succeeded his father Vespasian upon his death, becoming the first Roman emperor to succeed his biological father. Titus's reign was marked by significant public works and military campaigns, including the Siege of Jerusalem, which ended with the destruction of the Second Temple.

As emperor, Titus was known for his generosity and kindness, particularly towards the poor and the Jewish community. He also oversaw the construction of several public buildings, including the Colosseum and the Theater of Titus, which became iconic landmarks of Rome.

Titus's legacy extends beyond his own reign, as his family's influence continued to shape Roman politics and society for generations to come. His nephew, Domitian, succeeded him as emperor and continued many of Titus's policies.

In the years following Titus's death, his reputation as a wise and just ruler solidified, and he became an important figure in Roman history, remembered for his compassion and architectural achievements.
